Each detail said the write scope conflicts with a live claim held by the run that same call had created: r-20260926T140559747789 (pid 3815290) and r-20260926T140535589201. Each was launched, live, and the only review of its target. A captured output is at /tmp/claude-39486/-home-ITER-mcintos-Code-reckon/bd47f8f3-7617-4973-86e9-6be0d83c0a53/scratchpad/rv-landing-tests-measure-the-landing.json. First reproduce it at base through the dispatch entry point, under a temporary config home and a synthesised repository with the worker launch stubbed by a live pid: a dispatch whose write paths no other run claims returns ok:false with scope-conflict naming its own run id. Then name in the manifest the commit that introduced the post-launch check, found by reading git log for reckon/crew/dispatch.py, not by bisecting.

Done when a launched dispatch returns ok:true with its run_id and leaves exactly one live pointer; the post-launch scope check excludes the claim held by the run id this call created; and a real conflict still refuses, i.e. a second dispatch claiming the same path while the first run is live gets scope-conflict naming the first run. The real config home must be asserted untouched. At least one added assertion must fail at base. Measured files: tests/test_dispatch_launch_is_not_its_own_conflict.py (new) plus the existing test files that exercise dispatch scope conflicts, named in the manifest, in ONE invocation, with zero added failures against base. Report ruff findings on the staged paths against the count at base.
